requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case IS a complete and independent specification of the actions required to achieve a specific test purpose.
requirements.original: A test case is complete and independent specification of the actions required to achieve a specific test purpose.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case typically starts in a stable testing state and ends in a stable testing state.
requirements.original: It typically starts in a stable testing state and ends in a stable testing state.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case CAN involve one or more consecutive or concurrent connections to the SUT.
requirements.original: It may involve one or more consecutive or concurrent connections to the SUT.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case SHALL be complete in the sense that it is sufficient to enable a test verdict to be assigned unambiguously to each potentially observable test outcome.
requirements.original: The test case shall be complete in the sense that it is sufficient to enable a test verdict to be assigned unambiguously to each potentially observable test outcome (i.e. sequence of test events).

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case SHALL be independent in the sense that the derived executable test case can be executed in isolation from other test cases.
requirements.original: The test case shall be independent in the sense that it shall be possible to execute the derived executable test case in isolation from other such test cases.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case IS a special kind of function.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, test cases are a special kind of function.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case defines the behaviour that is executed to check whether the SUT passes a test or not.
requirements.original: Test cases define the behaviour, which have to be executed to check whether the SUT passes a test or not.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc
requirements.canonical: The behaviour of a test case IS performed by the MTC.
requirements.original: This behaviour is performed by the MTC which is automatically created when a test case is being executed.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc
requirements.canonical: The MTC IS created automatically when a test case is executed.
requirements.original: This behaviour is performed by the MTC which is automatically created when a test case is being executed.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case definition has the syntax `testcase` TestcaseIdentifier "(" [{(FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar) [","]}] ")" [`runs on` ComponentType] [`system` ComponentType] StatementBlock.
requirements.original:
testcase TestcaseIdentifier
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar) [","] } ] ")"
  [ runs on ComponentType ]
  [ system ComponentType ] 
  StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:verdict
requirements.canonical: The result of a test case execution IS a test verdict.
requirements.original: The result of a test case execution is a test verdict.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-header
requirements.canonical: A test case header IS composed of two parts: an interface part and a test system part.
requirements.original: A test case header has two parts:

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-header
requirements.canonical: The interface part of a test case header IS optional and IS denoted by the keywords `runs on`, which reference the required component type for the MTC.
requirements.original: a) interface part (optional): denoted by the keyword runs `on which references the required component type for` the MTC and makes the associated port names visible within the MTC behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: The port names of the component type referenced by the `runs on` clause of a test case ARE visible within the MTC behaviour.
requirements.original: a) interface part (optional): denoted by the keyword runs `on which references the required component type for` the MTC and makes the associated port names visible within the MTC behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc
requirements.condition: the runs on clause is missing
requirements.canonical: If the `runs on` clause of a test case is missing, the MTC created by the test case has no ports, no component constants and no component variables.
requirements.original: In case the runs `on clause` is missing, the MTC created by the test case has no ports, and no component constants and variables;

requirements.subject: ent:testcase-header
requirements.canonical: The test system part of a test case header IS optional and IS denoted by the keyword `system`, which references the component type that defines the required ports for the test system interface.
requirements.original: b) test system part (optional): denoted by the keyword system which references the component type which defines the required ports for the test system interface.

requirements.subject: ent:system-clause
requirements.condition: the test case has no system clause
requirements.canonical: The `system` clause of a test case SHALL only be omitted if only the MTC is instantiated during test execution.
requirements.original: The test system part shall only be omitted if, during test execution, only the MTC is instantiated.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence does not say whether a violation is a compile-time error or a runtime error, i.e. whether tools have to detect statically that a test case without system clause creates PTCs.
readings: A test case without a `system` clause that contains a `create` operation for a PTC SHALL be rejected at compile time.
Creating a PTC during the execution of a test case without a `system` clause SHALL cause a runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.condition: the system clause is omitted and the runs on clause is present
requirements.canonical: If the `system` clause of a test case is omitted and the `runs on` clause is present, the MTC type implicitly defines the test system interface ports.
requirements.original: In this case, the MTC type defines the test system interface ports implicitly if the runs `on clause is present.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.condition: both runs on and system clauses are missing
requirements.canonical: If both the `runs on` and the `system` clause of a test case are missing, the test system interface IS without ports.
requirements.original: If both runs` `on and system clauses are missing, the test system` interface has no ports;

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: The type of every formal parameter of a test case SHALL be a data type.
requirements.original: c) all formal parameter types of the test case shall be of a data type.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: The behaviour of a test case CAN be defined by using the program statements and operations described in clause 18.
requirements.original: The behaviour of a test case can be defined by using the program statements and operations described in clause 18.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case MAY be parameterized as described in clause 5.4.
requirements.original: Test cases may be parameterized as described in clause 5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case MAY be executed from a control behaviour definition.
requirements.original: Test cases can be executed from control behaviour definitions (see clause 26).

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: The formal parameter list of a test case SHALL follow the rules for formal parameter lists defined in clause 5.4.
requirements.original: a) The rules for formal parameter lists shall be followed as defined in clause 5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: A test case SHALL only be invoked with an `execute` statement in a function or altstep running on a control component.
requirements.original: b) Test cases may only be invoked with an execute statement in a function or altstep running on a control component as defined in clause 26.
